title: Revised Astra CT task: localized rejection establishes recognition disagreement beyond search
claim: Revised whole-volume Astra medium localized 3/6 reference instances and recovered 2/4 links, versus 2/6 and 1/4 originally, while entirely omitting a separate focus at both visits. In a fresh adaptive probe, exact center cues led to explicit normal/benign judgments for both reference-positive structures. Search alone is insufficient to explain the remaining omission; recognition/inclusion relative to GT remains a bottleneck, pending expert anatomy and image-only reference suitability review.
limitations: One case and one fresh attempt per condition; no causal prompt benefit or model ranking established.
Localized candidates are two visits of one adaptively selected positive reference focus; specificity is undefined.
Point cues change attention and prior belief as well as localization.
Explicit rejection establishes GT disagreement, not clinically adjudicated malignancy or a defective reference.
Mask quality conditional on target acceptance and complete event reasoning remain untested for the localized focus.
Fine abdominal reference partition remains under review; all frozen references and scores are retained.
Source annotators used clinical examination reports; the localized solver had CT and points only. Case-specific reports and clinical adjudication remain unavailable.
Offline controls reproduce a frozen verifier gap: judgment fields and masks are validated separately. The actual saved rejection and empty masks are consistent; original outcomes remain unchanged.
